lens: in-house builder: one part-time person shipping single-file GitHub Pages apps and Python jobs, no ops team; judged on technical risk on real LTA-style sheets (no layers, black pen weights 0.36-2.16 pt, several scales per page, outline text, 3,614-line hatching), sequencing, reuse of the 715 lines of spike code versus new invention, one-person maintainability, licence constraints (AGPL PyMuPDF, GPL LibreDWG, AGPL ultralytics, ODA non-commercial), and honesty of person-week estimates

scores.rationale: Effort curve 92/76/62 is the most conservative and its 6-month figure explicitly includes verification overhead, and every step is tied to the digest's 200/500-item gates; but nothing saves QS minutes before M3 shadow (week 18) and rule packs (week 24), because the M0 timer and CSV export are instrumentation, not savings. Money safety is the strongest of the five on provenance: every quantity cites sheet hash, viewport, confirmed scale, path ids and rule-pack version; no model emits a number; dimension grader blocks export outside 1%/5%; top-80%-of-value rule; rollback to Stage 2 on any money-bearing error. Feasibility is where it strains one part-time builder: it commits to two full implementations (import_pdf.py AND import-pdfjs.js, scale.py AND scale.js, kernel.py AND kernel.js, plus a scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting model exported to a hand-rolled JSON tree the browser evaluates), so every fix lands twice. The pdf.js clip stack for viewport reconstruction (intersecting clip polygons across save/restore) is not in extract_pdfjs.mjs (106 lines, no clip handling) and is budgeted at 3 person-weeks together with Bezier flattening and direction vectors on both routes, which is optimistic. The 42 person-weeks do sum correctly across milestones (2+4+2.5+5+4+3.5+5+4.5+3+8) but consume the full 0.4 FTE for two years with no slack. Cost is US$250/month, all open source, PyMuPDF confined to the batch job and pdf.js (Apache) in the QS-facing app, which is the right licence split. KKL fit is high: chainage ledger keyed to DR Capture chainage from/to so claims become lookups, confidentiality tier per project, rule packs from BQ preambles via the existing Extract agent, DR-keyed CSV rows.
scores.gets_right: Only design that specifies how to survive real sheets: viewports from get_drawings(extended=True) clip records with DBSCAN bbox-cluster fallback and title-text typing; a dimension-line detector (0.36 pt line with tick/arrow terminators and parallel numeric text) as a scale voter; quantised pen weight, dash, parallel-partner offset (double-wall pipe collapse, kerb face/back) and hatch-membership as classifier features; 'a detail or cross-section viewport is never a source of plan lengths'; synthetic regression via ezdxf PyMuPdfBackend DXF-to-PDF round trips; chainage ledger joined to DR Capture for monthly claims and VO diff as sheet.json revision diff.

scores.rationale: Curve 90/75/55: the 24-month 55% is the joint most aggressive and is admitted to be 'inference stacked on digest hour shares'; a large share of it rides on the claims roll-up reaching Stage 4 on all 30 contracts, which depends on DR data quality the design does not control. Gates are the digest's verbatim and per class x source, with the best-articulated confidence proxy of the five (check-pattern buckets whose empirical error is measured, not a weighted sum; missing check = sub-threshold). Money safety is strong: truth is 'QS final after chief-QS adjudication plus the workbook figure', not raw markups; engine never edits the QS's file, it writes a KKL-ENGINE layer on a copy; blind-then-reveal on 20%; automatic demotion. Feasibility for this builder is good in shape (a nightly Python job on an office PC over OneDrive-synced folders, JSONL/CSV to SharePoint, three PapaParse pages) and it avoids building a measurement canvas by letting the QS review engine proposals as annotations in Bluebeam; but the geometry engine 'on real sheets' is budgeted at 6 person-weeks (weeks 6-14) with far less specification than TrueLine of how viewports, scale and black-pen classification will be solved, and PyMuPDF xref_set_key writing of /Measure and /IT dictionaries plus pdf-lib annotation writing in the conditional Takeoff Pad are fiddly, under-documented work (digest: only the Line case is publicly documented). The whole premise is conditional on QSs saving measurement annotations, an open question in the digest; if not, Takeoff Pad (4 pw) precedes everything. Time to value: capture at week 6 produces data, not minutes; the first QS minutes saved arrive with assist at weeks 16-22, though the weekly scorecard can catch omissions before bids from month 3. Cost US$450/month including possible Bluebeam Core seats. KKL fit is the best: the 38-code Bluebeam tool chest mapped to DR Capture activity codes, CSVHEAD ingest, DuckDB local, T0/T1/T2 tiers enforced in the job, regression corpus of real sheets kept on SharePoint with only synthetic sheets in GitHub Actions (correct for OSA).
scores.gets_right: Assist mode delivered as an annotation layer on a PDF copy so QSs review in the tool they already use and the nightly diff is the corrections log; sheet fingerprint as SHA-256 of normalised get_cdrawings tuples so markups, engine runs and corrections pair automatically across re-saves; shadow scorer matching by shapely buffered overlap / IoU with reason codes that become the builder's weekly backlog; confidence calibrated per check pattern with >=200 items; confidential regression corpus on SharePoint, synthetic only in CI.

scores.rationale: Curve 101/95/84/65 is honest about being slow and its 24-month 65% depends on claims being 25-30% of QS hours (digest low-confidence inference) and on DR Capture rows carrying chainage, depth band and loads on >=90% of rows (design admits 'unverified'). It does not address the brief's daily drawing takeoff until month 9 and then compresses all of TrueLine's real-sheet work into a 16-week 'tender plug-in', so tender effort barely moves in year one. Money safety is structurally good for claims (two independent sources per line, surfaces as volume source with loads as KPI only, held lines never exported silently, named QS signs) but the design's own risk list concedes bulk excavation is often paid design-nett, in which case the survey engine yields evidence rather than the claim quantity, and truck-count reconciliation may never stabilise (digest: systematically unreliable). Feasibility for the code is fine (600 lines of lxml/scipy/numpy/shapely; the claims app is a single file), but the critical path is non-code: drone vendor procurement with NDA, CAAS operator/activity permits, Infrastructure Protection Act checks on MRT sites, MC surveyors accepting a shared surface, PDAL on a Windows office PC (conda-only in practice), and 'builder availability of ~2 d/wk for 12 months on this project alone', which contradicts part-time. Time to value: first assisted claims month 5-6 on 5 pilot contracts, gated on bq_map, flights and DR coverage. Cost is the outlier: US$7,500/month run cost (30x the others) driven by fortnightly RTK flights. KKL fit is deep on the site side (CSVHEAD fields, staging-ground tonnage by stream, asphalt by weight, SOPA cadence, JM packs) but weak on GeBIZ PDF takeoff and on 'learns from the takeoffs QSs already do'.
scores.gets_right: bq_map paid_on field (survey vs design_nett vs dr_rows vs tickets) per BQ item, which no other design makes explicit; joint-measurement pack with hashed surfaces and 10 random check cells for MC total-station verification; ticket/DO extraction confined to KKL's own tier-0 documents so cloud use is uncontroversial; calibrated bulking, m3/load and m3/h from survey-vs-loads residuals fed back into tender rates; asphalt reconciled by weighbridge tonnes because LTA M&W pays by weight.

scores.rationale: Curve 100/90/73/55: the 55% is aggressive, but the mechanism is the most credible because whole derived families (TRENCH, CHAMBER, RC-SECTION, PAVEMENT, KERB) graduate together on rulebook confirmation plus golden tests plus 300 clean lines rather than one primitive class at a time, and the digest's own inventory puts CIS RC build-ups (15%), trench runs and derived lines (15-20%) and BQ entry/reconciliation (15-20%) at roughly half of tender hours. The gate for derived lines is proportionate (deterministic code does not need a statistical accuracy gate; it needs rule confirmation and regression), and the primitives themselves pass through the digest's per-class x source gates later. Money safety: every rulebook parameter carries page citation and a named confirmer and an unconfirmed parameter blocks the engine; every line stamps engine version, rulebook version and primitive hash; judgement inputs stay human; garbage-in risk on typed primitives is real (one wrong IL propagates into 20 lines) and is mitigated by entry cross-checks (IL monotonic, depth within band, run totals vs schedule, scale grader) and the top-80%-of-value rule. Feasibility is the best fit to this builder: engine.js as one pure ES module used by the app, the claims page and node --test golden tests (including sample_drawing.truth.json), typed tables that mirror the QS's spreadsheet, .xlsx out via SheetJS, single-file pages, one on-prem Python harvester; per-milestone estimates are in builder-days (5, 6, 6, 5, 5, 6, 10, 8) and sum to about 11-12 person-weeks for the first six months, consistent with the stated 36 total; auto-measure is deliberately last, so all the real-sheet risk sits behind a working product. Time to value: TRENCH/CHAMBER in shadow on live tenders from week 6 (calc_trench.py already emits those lines), Stage 2 by month 3, BQ binder pre-filling the quantity sheet by week 11. Cost US$150/month, no new licences. KKL fit: item library keyed on DR Capture codes and struct/method/spec_element, claims join on the same keys with chainage-interval union against double claiming, VO pricing-basis column in the HKIS order, tier A/B/C with Tier-A rulebooks typed from templates.
scores.gets_right: Typed primitive tables as a day-one input path independent of any drawing parsing, so value does not wait on viewports, scale or classification; one engine module shared by browser app, claims roll-up and CI tests; rulebook parameters with {value, source_page, confirmed_by} and 'rulebook incomplete' blocking output; entry-time cross-checks that catch the garbage-in failure mode; CI blocking release when any golden line changes; automation order that puts deterministic families before measured primitives.

scores.rationale: Curve 97/88/74/58 with the candid note that section-based volumes cap the reduction near 40-45% of takeoff effort; gates are the digest's and enforced in the UI. Money safety is sound in principle (VLM emits labels, regions and cross-checks, never a quantity; per-viewport scale must be QS-confirmed and dimension check green before export; kerb type gate at 97% because 'type is the money'), but it lets VLM schedule reads (sizes, IL/GL, BBS totals, which are money-bearing attributes) reach Stage 3 by month 6 on a claimed 98% cell accuracy, against digest evidence of 25-37% recall and up to 56% hallucination on structured drawing extraction and Claude Opus 4 at 40% on dense dimension reads; and T1 crops of client drawings go to cloud models. Feasibility is the fatal weakness for one part-time builder: 76 person-weeks in the costs block (64 in its own text), a FastAPI runner with Entra ID sign-in (a server, outside house style), a four-model benchmark harness (Gemini 3 Pro via Vertex, Claude, GPT-5.x, local Qwen2.5-VL), a YOLO detector exported to ONNX and run with onnxruntime-web, PaddleOCR, a surface engine, a claims module and the canvas, all maintained by one person; 'canvas with counts and schedule reads in assist by week 7' requires the sheet model, viewport and scale problems solved in weeks 1-4, which TrueLine budgets at 6.5 weeks for the same work. Time to value is nominally early (schedule reads via the existing Extract agent are real) but counts and schedule reads are under 10% of tender hours. Cost US$600/month plus VM, Gemini lane and possible ultralytics or Artifex licences. KKL fit: the confidentiality gateway (T2 sessions never receive an API key, egress log per project) is the best treatment of OSA/NDA of the five; template library per client as data; annotated PDF export readable in Bluebeam; but the Gemini/Vertex lane fragments the Claude workbench KKL already has.
scores.gets_right: Confidentiality gateway as code (tier decides endpoint and content blocks, T2 sessions have no API key, every egress logged); cost readout per item (qty x KKL rate) so review attention follows money; annotated-PDF export with ISO 32000 /Measure and /Subj so the canvas output opens in Bluebeam; kerb-type classification as its own money gate; detector inference kept local via onnxruntime-web; honest cap on effort reduction from section-based volumes.

ranking: KKL Takeoff Overlay: the in-house civils.ai

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: Assist mode as a KKL-ENGINE annotation layer written onto a copy of the QS's PDF (PyMuPDF add_polyline_annot/add_polygon_annot with /Measure, /Subj = activity code, custom columns = checks and path ids), reviewed in Bluebeam, with the nightly diff between engine and final annotations as the corrections log
best_ideas_to_graft.why: Removes the need to build and maintain a measurement canvas in the first year; the QS stays in their own tool; the same 75-line extract_markups.py reader becomes both harvester and corrections diff

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: Sheet fingerprint = SHA-256 of normalised get_cdrawings tuples plus words, independent of annotations and re-saves; confidence as check-pattern buckets with empirical error measured per pattern (missing check = sub-threshold); shadow scorer matching engine items to QS markups by shapely buffered overlap / IoU with reason codes
best_ideas_to_graft.why: These are the three pieces that turn daily QS work into pairable labels, a calibrated auto-accept rule and a reason-coded backlog for one builder; all are small Python over libraries already in the spikes

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: Viewport reconstruction from get_drawings(extended=True) clip/scissor records with DBSCAN bbox-cluster fallback and title-text typing; per-viewport three-voter scale (title text corrected for page size, dimension-line detector, scale bar) with QS confirmation cached per originator template; pen-weight/dash/parallel-partner/hatch-membership classifier features; 'detail and section viewports never supply plan lengths or counts'
best_ideas_to_graft.why: This is the only concrete answer in the panel to the digest's real-sheet findings (no layers, black pens, several scales per page, 3,614 hatch lines); it should be the spec for the auto-measure phase, implemented once (PyMuPDF batch shadow), not twice

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: Synthetic regression suite via ezdxf drawing add-on PyMuPdfBackend (DXF with known quantities rendered to PDF and re-measured) plus a real-sheet corpus of >=30 sheets before any promise; chainage ledger of designed quantities per activity code per interval joined to DR Capture chainage from/to for monthly claims
best_ideas_to_graft.why: Cheap, deterministic test coverage the builder can run in CI without confidential sheets; the chainage ledger makes drain/kerb/pipe claim lines a lookup instead of a re-measure

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: Confidentiality gateway as code: per-project tier decides endpoint and permitted content blocks, T2 sessions never receive an API key, every egress logged to SharePoint; cost readout (qty x rate) on every item; annotated-PDF export with /Measure so outputs open in Bluebeam
best_ideas_to_graft.why: About 200 lines that make OSA/NDA compliance verifiable rather than procedural; the cost readout directs review attention to money and implements the top-80%-of-value rule visibly

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: bq_map paid_on field per BQ item (survey | design_nett | dr_rows | tickets) with measure_rule and band_edges; joint-measurement pack with hashed surfaces and random check cells; ticket/DO extraction confined to KKL's own tier-0 documents
best_ideas_to_graft.why: Makes the claims roll-up correct per contract preamble instead of assuming survey pays; the JM pack is a later, optional add-on once a contract funds a survey; ticket extraction reuses the existing Extract agent at zero confidentiality risk

best_ideas_to_graft.idea: Entry-time cross-checks on primitives (IL monotonic along a run, GL-IL depth within band range, run-length total vs drain schedule read with citations, scale-bar grader blocking export >5%) and 'rulebook incomplete' blocking any derived output until every money-bearing parameter is confirmed against its cited page
best_ideas_to_graft.why: The garbage-in failure mode (one bad level into twenty lines) is the main money risk of a calculation-first spine and these checks are cheap pure functions

fatal_flaws.flaw: Scope is a product team's roadmap, not a part-time builder's: 76 person-weeks (64 in its own text), a FastAPI server with Entra ID outside the single-file house style, a four-model VLM benchmark lane including Vertex/Gemini and a local Qwen2.5-VL, a YOLO-to-ONNX-to-browser pipeline, PaddleOCR, a surface engine, a claims module and the canvas; 'counts and schedule reads on the canvas by week 7' presumes viewport and scale resolution solved in weeks 1-4. One person cannot maintain this, and the VLM schedule reads promoted to Stage 3 by month 6 put money-bearing attributes (sizes, IL/GL) on the weakest evidence in the digest

Does not answer the brief for nine months (drawing takeoff is a 16-week plug-in in M7), while its critical path runs through things the builder cannot control: drone vendor procurement and CAAS/IPA permits, main-contractor acceptance of a shared surface, DR Capture chainage/loads coverage >=90% (unverified), and preambles that may pay bulk excavation design-nett; run cost US$7,500/month is 30x the other designs and 'builder 2 d/wk on this project alone' is not part-time

Conditional: the entire capture premise rests on QSs saving PDF measurement annotations, which the digest lists as an open question; if the week-1 sample says no, the design must first build the Takeoff Pad (4 pw, writing /Measure annotations with pdf-lib) and becomes a canvas design with a thinner real-sheet spec than TrueLine. Not fatal if the sample says yes

Not fatal, but a one-person maintenance trap: importer, scale resolver, measurement kernel and classifier evaluation are each specified twice (Python and JavaScript) with shared test vectors, and a scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting model must be exported to a hand-rolled JSON tree for the browser; combined with first QS savings at week 18-24, a stalled plan leaves a large half-built engine

unsupported_claims.claim: Claim 2: >=90% per-path precision on measurable classes after no more than 20 corrected sheets from the same originator, using pen weight, dash, parallel-partner, hatch membership, symbol signature and label regex
unsupported_claims.why_fragile: No evidence exists; the spike's sig() keys on stroke colour and closure on a synthetic sheet with no curves, hatching or overlaps, while real LTA sheets are all black with 3,614 hatch strokes and text drawn as glyph outlines; the digest says no civil dataset exists to pre-train on. The 3 person-week budget for a dual-route importer with clip-stack viewport reconstruction is also optimistic given extract_pdfjs.mjs has no clip handling today
